children: Shares of recently listed OnEMI Technology Solutions fell in Friday’s trade after the digital lending company declared a plan to raise up to Rs 832.19 crore through a preferential issue, with the proposed issue price set substantially above the price at which the company went public just over four months ago.
OnEMI Technology Solutions stocks traded 2.97 per cent lower at Rs 349 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in the morning session.

The board has approved the issue of up to 2.64 crore equity shares at Rs 314.11 apiece, implying a premium of around 84 per cent over the company’s IPO price of Rs 171. The proposed fundraise is subject to shareholder and other statutory and regulatory approvals.

The shares will be allotted to 34 identified non-promoter investors. Axis Small Cap Fund has been earmarked the largest allocation of 34.89 lakh shares, equivalent to 1.67 per cent of the company’s outstanding equity after the proposed issue. HDFC Banking & Financial Services Fund will receive 34.39 lakh shares, representing 1.65 per cent, while Massachusetts Institute of Technology will receive 25.46 lakh shares, or 1.22 per cent.

Other proposed investors include Axis Flexi Cap Fund, Axis Multi Cap Fund, Ashoka WhiteOak Emerging Markets Equity Fund, Envision India Fund, Groww Multi Cap Fund, Groww Small Cap Fund and HDFC Innovation Fund.
The proposed capital raise comes a little over four months after OnEMI Technology Solutions made its stock market debut on May 8.

The company’s Rs 926 crore IPO was priced at Rs 171 per share and the stock listed at a premium on both exchanges. The public issue included a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore, through which the company raised new capital.

The proposed preferential issue would therefore represent another significant capital infusion shortly after the IPO, with the company now seeking funds from a group of institutional and other identified investors at a considerably higher issue price.
On Thursday, the company’s shares closed at Rs 359.70, giving it a market capitalisation of around Rs 6,376 crore.

The proposed allotment includes several mutual fund schemes and institutional investors. Axis and HDFC mutual fund schemes account for some of the largest allocations, while MIT, WhiteOak, Groww and other investment entities are also participating.

As of September 11, Axis Small Cap Fund and Massachusetts Institute of Technology did not hold shares in OnEMI Technology Solutions. HDFC Banking & Financial Services Fund held 12.10 lakh shares, representing 0.67 per cent of the company’s equity, before the proposed preferential issue.

OnEMI Technology Solutions operates digital lending platform Kissht. The latest fundraise is aimed at strengthening the company’s capital position and supporting its next phase of growth, according to the company.
